source: public audit corpus — share calculation in deposit/withdraw
title: Share inflation via first-depositor donation
mechanism: When totalSupply==0 the first depositor sets the share price; by depositing 1 wei and then donating assets directly, the attacker inflates totalAssets so the next depositor's shares round to nearly zero, and the attacker redeems and captures the victim's deposit.
root_cause: share = assets * totalSupply / totalAssets uses the raw balance (donatable) and the first mint sets the exchange rate with no dead/virtual shares.
preconditions: deposit() mints shares as assets * totalSupply / totalAssets
totalAssets() reads address(this).balance / raw balance (donatable)
totalSupply()==0 at the attacker's first deposit
invariant: For any two sequential depositors D1, D2: shares(D2) * totalAssets / totalSupply after D1's redeem == D2's deposit (no value transfer from D2 to D1).
incorrect_behavior: D2's shares truncate toward zero because totalAssets is pre-inflated; D1 redeems D2's deposit as profit.
exploit_sequence: deposit 1 wei (becomes price-setter)
donate a large amount directly (totalAssets jumps)
victim deposits (shares = assets*1/totalAssets ~ 0)
redeem your shares; take the victim's deposited assets
impact: Complete loss of the next depositor's funds (often 100% of the deposit).
remediation: Mint dead shares/virtual offset on the first deposit, or track assets with an internal accounting variable updated only by deposit/redeem (never raw balance), or enforce a minimum meaningful first deposit.
code_evidence: function convertToShares(uint assets) public view returns (uint) { return assets * totalSupply / totalAssets(); } // totalAssets() = balanceOf(this)
corrected_code:
uint private _assets; // updated ONLY in deposit/redeem
function deposit(uint a) external { uint s = a * totalSupply / _assets; ... _assets += a; }
verification_evidence: Classic ERC4626 audit finding (OZ forum 'Ideal ERC4626'): a 1-wei first deposit + donation makes the second deposit unrecoverable. Reproduce in a foundry test: assert victim.balanceOf(token)==0 after attacker redeem.

source: public audit corpus — rounding direction favor
title: Round-down on deposit and redeem both favor the vault (user loss)
mechanism: A vault rounds DOWN shares when depositing AND rounds DOWN assets when redeeming, so every round-trip (deposit then withdraw the same amount) loses a dust amount to the vault; repeated, or large single ops, extract user value.
root_cause: Both conversion directions truncate instead of the standard favor-the-vault one-way (shares round down on deposit, assets round down on withdraw is actually standard, but an exploit arises when the same favor is combined with a second rounding in preview math or a fee).
preconditions: deposit mints floor(assets*rate) shares
withdraw burns floor(shares*rate) assets from user
no offsetting rounding direction or minimum output protection
invariant: round-trip monotonicity: redeem(deposit(a)) >= a - 1 wei (single rounding unit).
incorrect_behavior: each deposit->withdraw cycle loses rounding dust; an attacker cycles small amounts to drain accumulated dust, and large withdrawals lose a full rounding unit each.
exploit_sequence: deposit X (shares rounded down)
immediately withdraw all shares (assets rounded down)
repeat; accumulate the rounding dust + fee delta
impact: Small but repeatable loss per user; dust-siphoning if the vault also accumulates rounding residuals.
remediation: Apply the ERC4626 rounding-direction rules (round down shares on deposit, round DOWN assets on redeem — favor the vault, not the user); add a max loss/min out check; accumulate dust to the protocol, not to an arbitrary taker.
code_evidence: function withdraw(uint assets, address r) external returns (uint s) { s = assets * totalSupply / totalAssets(); _burn(r, s); } // both round down
verification_evidence: EIP-4626 security considerations: 'rounding can be exploited if both preview functions do not favor the protocol'. Foundry: assert withdraw(deposit(a)) < a for a dust-size a across repeated calls.

title: Deposit over-credit for fee-on-transfer tokens
mechanism: A vault credits the REQUESTED deposit amount while the fee-on-transfer token actually delivers less; users can withdraw the over-credited amount, draining the underlying.
root_cause: Ledger updated with msg value / requested amount instead of the measured balance delta received.
preconditions: integrated token charges a transfer fee (or is deflationary)
deposit() credits shares by the requested amount
withdrawal redeems against the inflated credit
invariant: sum(user shares) * exchange rate <= actual asset balance held by the vault at all times.
incorrect_behavior: shares credited exceed the assets actually received, so liabilities exceed real assets (insolvency).
exploit_sequence: deposit fee-on-transfer token repeatedly (credited full amount, received less each time)
withdraw the full credited amount
vault pays from its real holdings, becomes insolvent
impact: Vault insolvency; early withdrawers drain later depositors' funds.
remediation: Measure balanceOf(this) before and after the transfer and credit the delta; whitelist standard tokens or build fee-tolerant accounting.
code_evidence: function deposit(uint amt) external { token.transferFrom(msg.sender, address(this), amt); shares[msg.sender] += amt; } // over-credits
verification_evidence: Known pattern in ERC4626 integration audits: transfer fee ~1% makes share value < assets deposited. Foundry: deposit with a fee token, assert vault.balanceOf < sum deposits.

title: Division-before-multiplication truncation in collateral/price math
mechanism: A formula computes (a / b) * c or a / b * c where integer division truncates first, losing precision that can be exploited with chosen values (e.g. 1e18-scale collateral ratios).
root_cause: Intermediate division truncates before the multiplication restores scale, so the result is lower than the exact value by up to b-1 units — at 1e18 scale that is a material rounding loss.
preconditions: a formula performs division before multiplication in a value-bearing computation
the operands are user-influenced (amounts, prices, decimals)
the truncation is not compensated by a rounding-up adjustment
invariant: computed value must round in favor of the protocol (never below the true value for liabilities, never above for assets).
incorrect_behavior: borrow limits / collateral values / rewards come out slightly-to-materially too high or too low, enabling over-borrow or under-payment.
exploit_sequence: choose amounts that maximize the truncation error
borrow/withdraw against the inflated value
unwind; keep the difference
impact: Value leakage per transaction; over time or in bulk, meaningful loss.
remediation: Multiply first then divide (or use a math lib like FullMath / PRBMath), and add explicit rounding-up for values that must not understate liabilities.
verification_evidence: Standard Solidity math audit checklist (SWC-101 family). Foundry: pass amount just below 1e18 and assert the bad formula loses `price - 1` units.

source: public incident corpus — collateral valuation at manipulated spot price
title: Collateral valued from protocol-influenced spot oracle (overvaluation)
mechanism: A protocol's own large collateral deposit moves the on-chain oracle price of that asset; borrow limits scale with the inflated collateral, so one user can borrow the entire pool against their own token.
root_cause: Collateral value is a function of a spot price the depositor can move with the deposit itself (no depth/manipulation resistance).
preconditions: oracle price derives from the protocol's own deposit ratio
borrow limit = f(collateral value at that price)
attacker controls a large supply of the collateral asset
invariant: collateral value used for borrow limits must reflect an externally verifiable, manipulation-resistant price (TWAP/depth-weighted).
incorrect_behavior: depositing 1B of a token raises its on-chain price, inflating the attacker's collateral value and borrow limit far above real value.
exploit_sequence: deposit a huge amount of a low-value token you own
oracle price rises with the deposit
borrow max against the inflated collateral
default; the loss is socialized to depositors
remediation: Use manipulation-resistant oracles (TWAP, external price sources), cap borrow against own-token collateral, and weight collateral value by pool depth.
code_evidence:
// price is the protocol's own mark price updated by the deposit itself
uint collateralValue = collateralAmount * markPrice / 1e18;
corrected_code: uint collateralValue = collateralAmount * getTWAP(collateralAsset) / 1e18; // external, time-weighted
verification_evidence: Public postmortem: Mango $114M loss followed the exact deposit->price->borrow sequence.

source: public audit corpus — liquidation math / bad-debt socializing
title: Liquidation threshold/penalty math lets a position stay undercollateralized
mechanism: The liquidation penalty is added to the debt, but the collateral released / debt repaid computation rounds or under-covers the penalty, so liquidators are disincentivized and bad debt accrues to the protocol (socialized to depositors).
root_cause: liquidation math fails to fully cover debt + penalty, or the health-factor threshold is not enforced before and after partial liquidation.
preconditions: health factor = collateral / (debt * liquidationThreshold)
partial liquidation computes repay vs collateralReceived with rounding/penalty mismatch
no check that post-liquidation HF is above 1
invariant: after any liquidation, the position must remain collateralized (HF >= 1) OR be fully closed; total debt repaid + penalty == collateral released * price.
incorrect_behavior: a position can be liquidated repeatedly leaving HF < 1, growing bad debt that depositors absorb.
exploit_sequence: borrow to just above the liquidation threshold
let price dip slightly
liquidators find the penalty math leaves the position still undercollateralized
bad debt grows; depositors lose
impact: Protocol bad debt; depositor losses equal to the shortfall.
remediation: Round the penalty UP and the repayable amount DOWN so a liquidation always increases HF; cap partial liquidation so it cannot keep a position under water.
code_evidence:
uint debtRepaid = amount; // no penalty coverage
uint collatTaken = debtRepaid * price / 1e18;
verification_evidence: Aave/Compound liquidation spec: liquidators must always profit and HF must not worsen. Foundry: assert post-liquidation HF >= 1.0 in a price-sweep test.

source: public audit corpus — debt/interest accrual time math
title: Interest accrual with block-timestamp arithmetic (wrong or exploitable delta)
mechanism: Debt grows with (now - lastAccrual) * rate; if the delta can be zero, negative, or driven by a user-controlled timestamp, interest is not accrued (or a miner can delay accrual to pay less), breaking debt accounting.
root_cause: Accrual uses block.timestamp deltas that are not monotonic-guarded, or accrual is skip-able when the delta rounds to zero.
preconditions: interest = debt * ratePerSecond * (now - lastAccrued)
the rate or delta is user-influenceable, or accrual only runs on the borrower's own calls
small deltas round to zero interest
invariant: debt owed at time T >= debt at T0 * (1 + rate)^(T-T0) (no interest can be skipped).
incorrect_behavior: borrowers pay zero or less interest by timing calls so the accrual delta is tiny/zero, or accrual is not global.
exploit_sequence: borrow when the rate delta window yields zero interest
let the accrual skip (call paths that don't trigger global accrual)
repay principal without meaningful interest
impact: Interest income lost; lender yield underpaid; debt accounting drifts.
remediation: Accrue interest globally before any state-changing call (every external entry), use a minimum accrual step, and never let a borrower control the accrual timestamp.
code_evidence: function borrow(uint a) external { if (lastAccrued != block.timestamp) { debt += debt * rate * (block.timestamp - lastAccrued); lastAccrued = block.timestamp; } ... }
corrected_code:
modifier accrue() { _accrue(); _; } // applied to EVERY external entry point
function _accrue() internal { uint d = block.timestamp - lastAccrued; if (d > 0) { debt = debt * _rate.pow(d); lastAccrued = block.timestamp; } }
verification_evidence: Known lending-audit pattern (Compound borrow interest accrual). Foundry: assert accrued interest over N blocks == N * per-block rate even when only the borrower acts.

source: public audit corpus — reward distribution rounding to zero
title: Reward-per-share rounding truncates small stakers to zero
mechanism: Rewards accumulate as rewardPerShare in 1e18 fixed-point, but a user with a small stake has earned = stake * rewardPerShare / 1e18 which truncates; with low reward rates or small stakes, repeated claims pay zero and the residual is stuck or extractable.
root_cause: reward = accumulatedPerShare * stake / 1e18 truncates toward zero with no minimum-payout or accumulated-dust handling.
preconditions: rewards use per-share accumulator in fixed point
user stake small relative to 1e18 / rewardPerShare
claim() computes earned - paid with the same truncation
invariant: every user's cumulative claimed rewards == floor(accumulatedReward * stake / totalStake) and no staker is systematically excluded.
incorrect_behavior: small stakers can never claim (earned always rounds to 0), or an attacker creates many dust accounts to trap residual rewards.
exploit_sequence: stake a small amount
let rewards accumulate slowly
claim repeatedly; earned rounds to zero each time
(or) create many dust positions to trap protocol rewards
impact: Rewards stuck; small stakers economically excluded; residual value trapped.
remediation: Track reward debt per user precisely, use 1e36+ accumulator precision, and/or accumulate dust to a protocol treasury instead of dropping it.
code_evidence: function claim() external { uint earned = balance[msg.sender] * accPerShare / 1e18 - paid[msg.sender]; paid[msg.sender] += earned; transfer(earned); }
corrected_code:
// use higher precision accumulator and per-user reward debt (not balance snapshots)
uint256 internal constant PRECISION = 1e36;
verification_evidence: MasterChef-style reward rounding audit pattern. Foundry: stake 1 wei, accrue 1e18 rewardPerShare over time, assert claim returns 0 unless precision is raised.

source: public audit corpus — exchange-rate from manipulable reserves
title: Exchange-rate manipulation via direct reserve transfer (no fee accounting)
mechanism: An asset's exchange rate reads pool reserves directly (amount0/amount1) or token balanceOf(pool); an attacker donates/removes reserves (or uses a large swap on a thin pool) to move the rate used for conversions, minting or redeeming at a skewed price.
root_cause: Exchange rate derives from raw reserves that a donor/large-swapper can move in one transaction; no TWAP, no fee-on-transfer correction, no deviation bound.
preconditions: exchangeRate() = balanceA / balanceB (raw)
conversion/mint/redeem uses that rate in the same transaction as a large swap
pool is thin or donations count toward reserves
invariant: the exchange rate used for user conversions must not be movable by a single transaction's donation or thin-pool swap.
incorrect_behavior: a single tx donates to or drains one reserve, then mints/redeems at the skewed rate to extract the other asset.
exploit_sequence: donate asset A to the pool (reserves shift)
convert/mint using the skewed rate (receive too much B)
or: swap large on a thin pair, then redeem against the moved rate
unwind
impact: Direct value extraction from conversions, mints, or redemptions.
remediation: Use time-weighted average reserves/price, exclude donations from the rate (track internal reserve deltas), or enforce deviation bounds against an external price.
code_evidence: function exchangeRate() public view returns (uint) { return tokenA.balanceOf(this) * 1e18 / tokenB.balanceOf(this); }
corrected_code:
// track reserves via internal accounting updated only on swap/mint/burn
function exchangeRate() public view returns (uint) { return _reserveA * 1e18 / _reserveB; }
verification_evidence: Standard AMM read-only/oracle finding. Foundry: donate A, assert exchangeRate moved by > tolerance, then assert a mint at that rate extracts value.

source: public audit corpus — stale oracle valuation of assets
title: Collateral valued at a stale oracle price (under/over-valuation)
mechanism: A protocol prices collateral/debt with latestRoundData but ignores updatedAt/staleness, so a frozen feed continues to be trusted: over-valuation lets users borrow too much, under-valuation triggers unfair liquidations.
root_cause: No staleness check on the oracle feed; the protocol trusts any round regardless of age.
preconditions: price feed can go stale (chainlink heartbeat elapses)
borrow/liquidate reads the price with no updatedAt guard
no deviation-bound fallback
invariant: every value-bearing price used must be from a round younger than the freshness window (and within deviation bounds of a second source).
incorrect_behavior: a stale price (from before a real move) is treated as current — over- or under-valuing positions.
exploit_sequence: (over-valuation) feed goes stale high -> borrow against it -> price corrects -> default
(under-valuation) feed stale low -> healthy users get liquidated at a discount
impact: Bad debt or unfair liquidations; direct user loss.
remediation: require(updatedAt >= block.timestamp - MAX_STALE) and sanity/deviation bounds; consider a fallback oracle.
code_evidence:
(, int256 price, , , ) = feed.latestRoundData();
uint collateralValue = amount * uint(price) / 1e8; // no staleness check
verification_evidence: Chainlink secure-development practices; reproduced in audits (e.g. UST depeg: stale/collapsed LUNA price). Foundry: mock latestRoundData with an old updatedAt and assert the guard reverts.

source: public audit corpus — asymmetric balance accounting (balance inconsistency)
title: Asymmetric debit/credit writes desynchronize the balance ledger
mechanism: One code path adds to a user balance without the matching subtraction on the corresponding exit path (or vice versa), so sum(balances) drifts from the real asset holdings and users can mint value from the skew.
root_cause: Writes to the accounting ledger are not symmetric across all entry/exit paths — a path credits without the paired debit, or vice versa.
preconditions: multiple functions write the same balance mapping
an entry path credits without a corresponding exit-path debit
or an exit path debits without the paired entry credit
invariant: sum(balances) == trackedAssets always; no function may add or remove from one side without the exact mirror on the other.
incorrect_behavior: an attacker exploits the asymmetric path to inflate their balance (or zero a liability) without the matching real flow.
exploit_sequence: call the asymmetric entry path (credit without debit) repeatedly
use the inflated balance to withdraw/convert real assets
drain
impact: Minted value / insolvency proportional to the skew.
remediation: Every balance write must have a mirror write on the opposite path; prefer a single transfer/accounting module with one place that mutates balances.
code_evidence:
function donate() external { balance[msg.sender] += msg.value; } // credit with no real inflow to liabilities
function withdraw(uint a) external { require(balance[msg.sender] >= a); balance[msg.sender] -= a; send(a); } // debit exists
corrected_code:
// track total liabilities in lockstep; donate() credits the same ledger the
// withdraw() debits and the contract can never pay out more than it holds
verification_evidence: Audit finding class 'accounting desync'; reproducible by asserting sum(balances)==holdings before/after the asymmetric path. Foundry test included in the report.
